Fixed terminal rendering bug: lines disappearing when text exceeds viewport. Root cause: term.open() was called on a hidden wrapper (display:none), so xterm.js measured 0 font/cell dimensions, causing wrong row count. Fix: (1) wrapper made visible before term.open() by setting active class immediately, (2) removed .xterm position:absolute override that conflicted with xterm.js internal viewport layout, replaced with height:100%, (3) replaced setTimeout timing hacks with requestAnimationFrame, (4) removed forced scrollToBottom on every PTY output chunk.

Fixed terminal scrolling bug (content sinks off-screen instead of scrolling). Root cause: Tauri CSP (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self') silently blocked xterm.js and xterm.css CDN loads from cdn.jsdelivr.net. Without xterm.css, .xterm-viewport had no position:absolute/top:0/bottom:0 constraints, so it grew infinitely. Fix: downloaded xterm.min.js (283KB), xterm.css (5KB), xterm-addon-fit.min.js (2KB) into adt-console/src/vendor/ and updated index.html to use local paths. CSP now allows them as 'self' resources.

POSTMORTEM: Terminal scrolling bug (content sinks off-screen). SYMPTOM: Terminal fills correctly top-to-bottom. Once vertical space is full, instead of scrolling, entire content block moves DOWN line-by-line until all text exits through the bottom, leaving black screen. ROOT CAUSE: Tauri CSP in tauri.conf.json (line 32) sets script-src and style-src to 'self' only. xterm.js (v5) and xterm.css were loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net -- silently blocked by CSP. Without xterm.css, the .xterm-viewport element (which needs position:absolute; top:0; bottom:0 from xterm.css) defaults to position:static with auto height, so it grows infinitely instead of constraining to the .xterm parent. xterm.js internal scrolling depends on .xterm-viewport being height-constrained. WHY SILENT: CSP violations only appear in browser devtools console (not visible in Tauri unless devtools opened). No JS error thrown -- xterm.js was also blocked, so no terminal functionality at all in strict CSP. In some builds it partially worked from browser cache. FIX: Downloaded xterm.min.js, xterm.css, xterm-addon-fit.min.js into adt-console/src/vendor/. Updated index.html to reference vendor/ paths instead of CDN. Files are now embedded in Tauri binary via frontendDist and pass CSP as 'self' resources. PREVENTION: Never use CDN links in Tauri apps. All frontend dependencies must be vendored locally in src/vendor/. Tauri CSP 'self' means only files embedded in the app bundle are allowed.

rationale: Root cause of all Gemini (and all) sessions showing blank terminal FOUND. ipc.rs CreateSessionRequest uses #[serde(rename = "reservedSessionId")] but sessions.js create() was sending reserved_session_id (snake_case). Rust got None, generated its own session ID, emitted pty-output-<rust_id>. Frontend subscribed to pty-output-<reservedUUID>. Complete mismatch — zero PTY output ever received. FIX: sessions.js:125 reserved_session_id → reservedSessionId. Also added defensive re-listener in terminal.js activate() for ID-mismatch fallback. pty.rs oauth_creds fix already applied (REQ-067), needs Console rebuild to activate.

description: Gemini blank-terminal root cause: gemini CLI hangs silently for 60+ seconds when run as agent OS user (uid 995). Reproduced manually: as human user with sandbox HOME, gemini --version prints 0.33.0 in <30s; as agent user, zero output for 60s+. Suspected cause: agent /etc/passwd homedir is /home/agent which does not exist, and gemini-cli-core projectRegistry.getShortId tries to mkdir homedir-derived paths on startup. Workaround applied: renamed ~/.adt/production_mode -> ~/.adt/production_mode.disabled.20260503 so is_production_mode() returns false and PTY spawns as human user, not via sudo -u agent. Also during this work: added Claude credential block to pty.rs (.credentials.json + .claude.json + symlinks), bumped Gemini oauth_creds mode to 0o666, rebuilt Tauri binary (was Apr 30 stale), added /etc/sudoers.d/adt-no-use-pty with Defaults>agent !use_pty. FOLLOWUP NEEDED: properly create /home/agent owned by agent:dttp 700 OR fix gemini project registry to respect HOME env over passwd homedir, then re-enable production mode for proper privilege isolation.

authority: SPEC-048 task_299/task_301 — race condition in event listener registration
rationale: Fixed race condition: event.listen() is async IPC but was not awaited in prepare(), create(), and activate(). Gemini sessions showed blank terminal because the banner output arrived before the listener was registered. Made prepare(), create(), activate() async and added await on all event.listen() calls and all TerminalManager call-sites in sessions.js.

action_data.root_cause: event.listen() Promise not awaited — listener not registered when PTY emits first bytes
action_data.symptom: Gemini sessions showed blank terminal (Claude less affected due to slower startup)
action_data.fix: async/await on prepare(), create(), activate() and all call-sites

authority: Human urgent override — jurisdiction exception logged. Root cause analysis required SA investigation of terminal.js/sessions.js.
rationale: Root cause of Gemini blank terminal CORRECTLY identified: xterm.js write() before open() feeds the parser state machine but nothing renders until open(). Gemini TUI clear-screen sequences execute in the buffer; when open() fires xterm renders post-clear blank state. Claude is unaffected because it starts slowly. Fix: prepare() now sets _opened=false, _pending=[] on the entry; listener buffers data to _pending until _opened is true; activate() calls term.open() then sets _opened=true and flushes _pending to term. Previous fix (async event.listen) was correct but addressed the wrong bug.

action_data.root_cause: write() before open() in xterm.js — TUI clear-screen sequences in buffer cause blank render on open()
action_data.previous_fix: async event.listen (correct but not the root cause)
action_data.symptom: Gemini sessions blank after rebuild; Claude unaffected (slow startup means open() called first)
action_data.fix: Buffer PTY data in entry._pending until entry._opened=true; flush to term immediately after term.open()

Fixed blank Gemini terminal (5th occurrence). Root cause: fitAddon.fit() was async (rAF ~16ms) so xterm.js was 80x24 when Gemini first drew its TUI at PTY size, causing size mismatch; SIGWINCH from show() 100ms timeout triggered Gemini clear+redraw but if Gemini went idle between clear and draw the screen stayed blank. Fix: (1) terminal.js activate()/create(): synchronous getBoundingClientRect()+fitAddon.fit()+syncSize() immediately after term.open() so xterm.js is correct size before first output; (2) terminal.js activate(): 250ms delayed replay() as safety net; (3) sessions.js create()/spawnChild(): measure #terminal-container rect and compute cols/rows from char metrics (9.6px/19.2px) instead of hardcoded 120x30, so PTY starts at actual terminal size.

Fixed blank Gemini terminal (6th+ occurrence). Root cause identified: THREE SIGWINCHs fired within 100ms of session creation: (1) activate() immediate syncSize, (2) activate() rAF syncSize 16ms later, (3) show() 100ms timer syncSize. Each SIGWINCH made Gemini clear+redraw. replay() at 250ms fired mid-clear from SIGWINCH #3, so ring buffer ended with a clear-screen and no TUI. Fix: (1) Removed rAF syncSize from activate() — keep only term.focus(). (2) Added _justActivated flag: activate() sets it true, show() skips syncSize when true and clears it. Result: exactly ONE SIGWINCH per new session. (3) Delayed replay from 250ms to 2000ms — enough time for Gemini to finish all redraws. (4) Moved _pending flush to BEFORE syncSize so xterm.js has old TUI before Gemini clears.

WebKit attempts to load http://127.0.0.1:1430/ on every launch and fails. Fix: rebuild binary with current config. NOT a service-launch race (5001/5002 are up and serving), NOT an iframe issue, NOT SPEC-054 territory. description: FINDING: Binary reverse-engineering summary. agy v1.0.9 is a stripped PIE Go binary from google3/third_party/jetski/ codebase. Key packages: cortex/customization/hooks/jsonhook (hook parser), cortex/customizations (aggregator), hooks/hookcaller (executor). HookHandler fields: type string, command string, args []string, cwd string, timeout int. Schema progression: phase1=array(WRONG), phase2=single object no name(0 handlers), phase3=named wrapper+PreToolUse(1 handler, CORRECT). Global config/hooks.json uses SAME named-hook schema as plugin hooks.json.

description: FINDING: spec-jurisdiction-gap. DTCP gates writes by intersecting candidate_path with active_spec.paths[], ignoring the role-jurisdiction set defined in AI_PROTOCOL.md section 2. Result: any role attempting to write within its OWN designated directories is denied whenever the current active_spec does not happen to enumerate those paths. Today this fired at least 3 times: pty.rs 21:22 (DevOps path under SPEC-061 not SPEC-062), log_event.py 20:35 (Backend path), and _cortex/reports/ at 21:48 (Overseer path). Each was resolved via operator_bypass_edit, eroding the gating signal. Recommended fix: DTCP should permit a write when EITHER active_spec authorizes the path OR the actor role's standing jurisdiction includes the path. Role jurisdiction is the floor, active_spec is the focusing lens, not a replacement. Priority: high; this misfire pattern is currently the main source of operator bypasses today.

action_data.recommended_fix: DTCP policy.py: permit if active_spec authorizes path OR role.jurisdiction includes path

# SPEC-067: Forge Wizard

**Status:** APPROVED
**Author:** Systems_Architect (CLAUDE)
**Date:** 2026-06-26
**Complements:** SPEC-043 (Forge), SPEC-062 D5 (Task creation), SPEC-062-F (Verification)
**Tier:** Operational
**Priority:** HIGH — operator's first contact with the framework currently dead-ends in TODO templates

**Intent:** Replace the silent "Forge Application" button with a minimal multi-step wizard that captures *just enough* intent (5 short fields) for an autonomous Architect agy worker to (a) fill `SPEC-001_VISION.md` with real content, (b) derive 3-7 child specs (platform / data plane / interaction surface / etc. as appropriate for the wish), and (c) leave each child spec ready for `/decompose`. The wizard shows live progress while the Architect runs and ends on a "Open Spec Map" call-to-action with a populated tree. No more empty `TODO:` Vision specs and no more decompose workers producing meta-tasks like "Write the Problem section."

**Triggering Event:** CEV-OP-006 — 2026-06-26 operator built an "eyetoy" project: typed wish text into the Forge wizard, pressed Forge Application, project scaffolded but SPEC-001 came back as the raw template with `TODO:` placeholders. Decomposing produced conceptual tasks like "Write Vision section" because the wish text was stored in a Capability Intent record nobody reads. The whole flow appeared to do nothing useful.

**Success Condition:** Operator opens Forge wizard, fills 2 short screens (5 fields total, 3 required), presses Forge. Within 90s the wizard shows: project scaffolded, SPEC-001 filled, N child specs created. Operator clicks "Open Spec Map" and lands on a populated tree where every node is decomposable. SPEC-001's Problem / Vision / Users / Scope / Success Criteria / Constraints sections contain substantive content extracted from the operator's wish, not `TODO:` placeholders. Child specs each have a one-paragraph Intent and a Success Condition derived from §5 of SPEC-001.

---

## 1. Wizard UI (2 steps, 5 fields)

`adt-console/src/js/launcher.js` `openForgeWizard()` becomes a 2-screen flow:

**Screen 1 — The Wish (existing, slightly tightened):**

* **What do you want to build?** *(required, textarea)* — placeholder: "An eyetoy-style game where the onboard camera tracks the player's hands to move a virtual ball on screen."
* **Project path** *(required, text)*
* **Project name** *(optional; derived from path basename)*

**Screen 2 — Completeness signals (3 quick prompts):**

* **Who is this for?** *(required, one line)* — placeholder: "Casual home players, ages 8+, single-player at first."
* **What does 'done v1' look like?** *(required, one line)* — placeholder: "Player can stand in front of the camera, see their hand silhouette, and bat a ball that bounces off the screen edges."
* **Anything that's explicitly NOT in v1?** *(optional, one line)* — placeholder: "No multiplayer. No cloud sync. No mobile."
* **Hard constraints?** *(optional, one line)* — placeholder: "Must run on Linux laptop with built-in webcam, no GPU required."

Two short screens, total 5 inputs, 3 of them required. No org chart, no risk matrix, no MoSCoW table.

## 2. Backend: extend `/governance/forge`

`adt_center/api/governance_routes.py` `api_forge_project()` accepts the additional fields:

```json
{
  "path": "...",
  "intent_description": "<wish>",
  "users":       "<screen 2 field 1>",
  "success_v1":  "<screen 2 field 2>",
  "out_of_scope":"<screen 2 field 3 - optional>",
  "constraints": "<screen 2 field 4 - optional>",
  "name": "..."
}
```

After project scaffold + DTCP start + Capability Intent record (all existing), the route does NEW work:

1. **Write a `forge_brief.json`** to the new project's `_cortex/ops/forge_brief.json` capturing all 5 inputs verbatim.
2. **Spawn an agy Architect worker** with the new `forge_prompts/architect.md` template (see §3). Worker is detached, log at `_cortex/ops/forge_worker.log`.
3. **Return immediately** with `{forge_session_id, project_name, status: "forging"}` — UI now polls progress instead of seeing a static success modal.

## 3. Forge Architect Prompt Template

NEW file `adt_center/api/forge_prompts/architect.md` (template format same as `decompose_prompts/architect.md`).

Two-phase prompt:

**Phase A — Fill SPEC-001:**

* Read `_cortex/ops/forge_brief.json` for the 5 inputs.
* Overwrite `_cortex/specs/SPEC-001_VISION.md` (currently template) with a filled version:
  * §1 Problem: 1 short paragraph extracted from `intent_description`
  * §2 Vision: 1 paragraph end-state description
  * §3 Users: from `users` field, ASCII bullets
  * §4 In Scope: 3-5 bullets derived from wish
  * §4 Out of Scope: from `out_of_scope` field (verbatim if provided; sensible defaults if not)
  * §5 Success Criteria: from `success_v1` field, restated as 2-4 observable checks
  * §6 Constraints: from `constraints` field (verbatim if provided)
  * §7 Open Questions: 2-4 honest unknowns the worker spotted while writing the above
* POST a `cross_ai_progress_update` ADS event: `{phase: "vision_filled", pct: 40}`.

**Phase B — Derive child specs:**

* Identify 3-7 child concerns that, together, deliver the §5 Success Criteria. Examples for eyetoy:
  * SPEC-002: Camera + Vision Pipeline
  * SPEC-003: Hand / Object Tracking
  * SPEC-004: Render Surface + Physics
  * SPEC-005: Game Loop + State
  * (optional) SPEC-006: Onboarding + Calibration
* For EACH child, run one curl against the spec-create endpoint (see §4):

```bash
curl -s -X POST 'http://localhost:5001/api/specs?project={project_name}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{{"spec_id":"SPEC-NNN","title":"...","intent":"<1 paragraph>","success_condition":"<observable test>","tier":"Operational","derived_from":"SPEC-001"}}'
```

* Between child specs, POST `cross_ai_progress_update` with monotonically increasing pct.
* When all children created, POST `cross_ai_task_complete` with `{result_summary, spec_ids_created}`.

The worker does NOT decompose any spec into tasks — that's a separate flow the operator triggers later. The wizard's job ends at "specs created."

## 4. New Backend Endpoint: Create Spec

`POST /api/specs` — accepts `{spec_id, title, intent, success_condition, tier, derived_from}`, writes `_cortex/specs/<spec_id>_<TITLE_UNDERSCORED>.md` with the project's spec markdown format, updates `config/specs.json`, emits `spec_created` ADS event.

If `spec_id` is omitted, server allocates the next free SPEC-NNN.

## 5. Wizard Live Progress

After Screen 2 submit, the modal switches to a Progress screen:

* Shows `<project_name> forging…` and a progress bar.
* Polls `GET /api/governance/forge/<forge_session_id>/status` every 2s — returns:
  ```json
  {"state": "forging", "phase": "vision_filled", "pct": 40,
   "specs_created": ["SPEC-001"], "log_tail": ["..."]}
  ```
* When `state == "complete"`: bar fills, screen flips to "Forge Complete" with:
  * List of spec IDs created (clickable to open in Spec Map)
  * Primary button: **"Open Spec Map"** (closes wizard, opens map on the new project's SPEC-001)
  * Secondary: **"Open in Panel"**
* If `state == "failed"`: red border, show error and worker log tail; primary button: **"Retry"** (re-spawns forge worker against same `forge_brief.json` — no data lost).

## 6. New Backend Endpoint: Forge Status

`GET /api/governance/forge/<forge_session_id>/status` — looks up the forge worker by session id, returns process state + ADS-derived progress (`cross_ai_progress_update` events filtered to this session) + spec_count (from filesystem scan).

## 7. ADS Schema Additions

`adt_core/ads/schema.py` — extend `FORGE_EVENTS` or add:

```python
FORGE_EVENTS = [
    "forge_initiated",          # path, intent, name
    "forge_brief_written",      # forge_session_id, fields_count
    "forge_worker_spawned",     # forge_session_id, pid
    "forge_vision_filled",      # forge_session_id, spec_id="SPEC-001"
    "forge_child_spec_created", # forge_session_id, spec_id, title
    "forge_complete",           # forge_session_id, spec_ids
    "forge_failed",             # forge_session_id, reason, log_path
]
```

## 8. Configuration Surface

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ADT_FORGE_TIMEOUT_SEC`  | 300  | Architect worker hard timeout |
| `ADT_FORGE_MODEL`        | `Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)` | Quality matters here |
| `ADT_FORGE_MIN_CHILDREN` | 3    | Floor on child spec count |
| `ADT_FORGE_MAX_CHILDREN` | 7    | Ceiling on child spec count |

## 9. Affected Paths

| Path | Role | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `adt-console/src/js/launcher.js` | Frontend | §1 two-screen wizard; §5 progress polling |
| `adt-console/src/css/launcher.css` | Frontend | progress bar + complete/failed states |
| `adt_center/api/governance_routes.py` | Backend | §2 forge endpoint extension; §4 spec-create endpoint; §6 status endpoint |
| `adt_center/api/forge_prompts/architect.md` | Backend | NEW — Phase A + B prompt template |
| `adt_core/ads/schema.py` | Backend | §7 FORGE_EVENTS constant |
| `_cortex/templates/project_bootstrap/SPEC-001_VISION.md.tmpl` | Architect | Leave intact — the worker overwrites it after scaffold |

## 10. Acceptance Criteria

* ✅ Operator submits wizard with eyetoy wish → within 90s sees "Forge Complete: SPEC-001, SPEC-002, SPEC-003, SPEC-004, SPEC-005 created".
* ✅ Opening SPEC-001 in spec map shows filled Problem/Vision/Users/Scope/Success sections (no `TODO:` strings).
* ✅ Opening any child spec shows a one-paragraph Intent and Success Condition that traces to SPEC-001 §5.
* ✅ Pressing Decompose on a child spec produces *technical* tasks (e.g. "implement camera capture pipeline"), not meta tasks ("write Problem section").
* ✅ Forge worker death (timeout, exit-1, killed) surfaces in wizard as red Failed state with log tail.
* ✅ Retry button on Failed state re-runs the worker without re-asking for inputs.

## 11. Rollout

Single phase, single PR — frontend + backend land together because the wizard depends on the new endpoints.

1. Backend: forge endpoint extension + spec-create + status (§2, §4, §6, §7).
2. Prompt template (§3).
3. Frontend: 2-screen wizard + live progress (§1, §5).
4. Smoke test: eyetoy wish → 5 specs created → spec map renders → child decompose produces technical tasks.

ETA: 6-8 hours focused.

## 12. Out of Scope (deferred)

* Operator editing of generated specs in the wizard itself — they can edit in the Panel afterwards.
* Auto-triggering decompose on each child spec — kept manual for v1 so operator reviews specs before tasks fan out.
* Sub-children (SPEC-002 spawning SPEC-002a/b) — keep tree flat for v1.
* Multi-architect contention (two forges at once on same path) — UI prevents this by checking project existence before spawn.

## 13. Cross-Spec Impact

* **SPEC-043 (Forge):** §2 extends the existing endpoint without breaking the old contract (new fields are optional).
* **SPEC-049 (CAOP):** the forge worker can reuse the CAOP task plumbing for progress reporting.
* **SPEC-062 D5 (Task creation):** unchanged — wizard creates specs only, not tasks.
* **SPEC-062-F (Verification):** child specs each gain `acceptance_criteria` placeholders the verifier will later check.
* **SPEC-064 (Standards):** out of scope here — operator can add `standards_refs[]` to any spec after forging.

# SPEC-067: Forge Wizard

**Status:** APPROVED
**Author:** Systems_Architect (CLAUDE)
**Date:** 2026-06-26
**Complements:** SPEC-043 (Forge), SPEC-062 D5 (Task creation), SPEC-062-F (Verification)
**Tier:** Operational
**Priority:** HIGH — operator's first contact with the framework currently dead-ends in TODO templates

**Intent:** Replace the silent "Forge Application" button with a minimal multi-step wizard that captures *just enough* intent (5 short fields) for an autonomous Architect agy worker to (a) fill `SPEC-001_VISION.md` with real content, (b) derive 3-7 child specs (platform / data plane / interaction surface / etc. as appropriate for the wish), and (c) leave each child spec ready for `/decompose`. The wizard shows live progress while the Architect runs and ends on a "Open Spec Map" call-to-action with a populated tree. No more empty `TODO:` Vision specs and no more decompose workers producing meta-tasks like "Write the Problem section."

**Triggering Event:** CEV-OP-006 — 2026-06-26 operator built an "eyetoy" project: typed wish text into the Forge wizard, pressed Forge Application, project scaffolded but SPEC-001 came back as the raw template with `TODO:` placeholders. Decomposing produced conceptual tasks like "Write Vision section" because the wish text was stored in a Capability Intent record nobody reads. The whole flow appeared to do nothing useful.

**Success Condition:** Operator opens Forge wizard, fills 2 short screens (5 fields total, 3 required), presses Forge. Within 90s the wizard shows: project scaffolded, SPEC-001 filled, N child specs created. Operator clicks "Open Spec Map" and lands on a populated tree where every node is decomposable. SPEC-001's Problem / Vision / Users / Scope / Success Criteria / Constraints sections contain substantive content extracted from the operator's wish, not `TODO:` placeholders. Child specs each have a one-paragraph Intent and a Success Condition derived from §5 of SPEC-001.

---

## 1. Wizard UI (2 steps, 5 fields)

`adt-console/src/js/launcher.js` `openForgeWizard()` becomes a 2-screen flow:

**Screen 1 — The Wish (existing, slightly tightened):**

* **What do you want to build?** *(required, textarea)* — placeholder: "An eyetoy-style game where the onboard camera tracks the player's hands to move a virtual ball on screen."
* **Project path** *(required, text)*
* **Project name** *(optional; derived from path basename)*

**Screen 2 — Completeness signals (3 quick prompts):**

* **Who is this for?** *(required, one line)* — placeholder: "Casual home players, ages 8+, single-player at first."
* **What does 'done v1' look like?** *(required, one line)* — placeholder: "Player can stand in front of the camera, see their hand silhouette, and bat a ball that bounces off the screen edges."
* **Anything that's explicitly NOT in v1?** *(optional, one line)* — placeholder: "No multiplayer. No cloud sync. No mobile."
* **Hard constraints?** *(optional, one line)* — placeholder: "Must run on Linux laptop with built-in webcam, no GPU required."

Two short screens, total 5 inputs, 3 of them required. No org chart, no risk matrix, no MoSCoW table.

## 2. Backend: extend `/governance/forge`

`adt_center/api/governance_routes.py` `api_forge_project()` accepts the additional fields:

```json
{
  "path": "...",
  "intent_description": "<wish>",
  "users":       "<screen 2 field 1>",
  "success_v1":  "<screen 2 field 2>",
  "out_of_scope":"<screen 2 field 3 - optional>",
  "constraints": "<screen 2 field 4 - optional>",
  "name": "..."
}
```

After project scaffold + DTCP start + Capability Intent record (all existing), the route does NEW work:

1. **Write a `forge_brief.json`** to the new project's `_cortex/ops/forge_brief.json` capturing all 5 inputs verbatim.
2. **Spawn an agy Architect worker** with the new `forge_prompts/architect.md` template (see §3). Worker is detached, log at `_cortex/ops/forge_worker.log`.
3. **Return immediately** with `{forge_session_id, project_name, status: "forging"}` — UI now polls progress instead of seeing a static success modal.

## 3. Forge Architect Prompt Template

NEW file `adt_center/api/forge_prompts/architect.md` (template format same as `decompose_prompts/architect.md`).

Two-phase prompt:

**Phase A — Fill SPEC-001:**

* Read `_cortex/ops/forge_brief.json` for the 5 inputs.
* Overwrite `_cortex/specs/SPEC-001_VISION.md` (currently template) with a filled version:
  * §1 Problem: 1 short paragraph extracted from `intent_description`
  * §2 Vision: 1 paragraph end-state description
  * §3 Users: from `users` field, ASCII bullets
  * §4 In Scope: 3-5 bullets derived from wish
  * §4 Out of Scope: from `out_of_scope` field (verbatim if provided; sensible defaults if not)
  * §5 Success Criteria: from `success_v1` field, restated as 2-4 observable checks
  * §6 Constraints: from `constraints` field (verbatim if provided)
  * §7 Open Questions: 2-4 honest unknowns the worker spotted while writing the above
* POST a `cross_ai_progress_update` ADS event: `{phase: "vision_filled", pct: 40}`.

**Phase B — Derive child specs:**

* Identify 3-7 child concerns that, together, deliver the §5 Success Criteria. Examples for eyetoy:
  * SPEC-002: Camera + Vision Pipeline
  * SPEC-003: Hand / Object Tracking
  * SPEC-004: Render Surface + Physics
  * SPEC-005: Game Loop + State
  * (optional) SPEC-006: Onboarding + Calibration
* For EACH child, run one curl against the spec-create endpoint (see §4):

```bash
curl -s -X POST 'http://localhost:5001/api/specs?project={project_name}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{{"spec_id":"SPEC-NNN","title":"...","intent":"<1 paragraph>","success_condition":"<observable test>","tier":"Operational","derived_from":"SPEC-001"}}'
```

* Between child specs, POST `cross_ai_progress_update` with monotonically increasing pct.
* When all children created, POST `cross_ai_task_complete` with `{result_summary, spec_ids_created}`.

The worker does NOT decompose any spec into tasks — that's a separate flow the operator triggers later. The wizard's job ends at "specs created."

## 4. New Backend Endpoint: Create Spec

`POST /api/specs` — accepts `{spec_id, title, intent, success_condition, tier, derived_from}`, writes `_cortex/specs/<spec_id>_<TITLE_UNDERSCORED>.md` with the project's spec markdown format, updates `config/specs.json`, emits `spec_created` ADS event.

If `spec_id` is omitted, server allocates the next free SPEC-NNN.

## 5. Wizard Live Progress

After Screen 2 submit, the modal switches to a Progress screen:

* Shows `<project_name> forging…` and a progress bar.
* Polls `GET /api/governance/forge/<forge_session_id>/status` every 2s — returns:
  ```json
  {"state": "forging", "phase": "vision_filled", "pct": 40,
   "specs_created": ["SPEC-001"], "log_tail": ["..."]}
  ```
* When `state == "complete"`: bar fills, screen flips to "Forge Complete" with:
  * List of spec IDs created (clickable to open in Spec Map)
  * Primary button: **"Open Spec Map"** (closes wizard, opens map on the new project's SPEC-001)
  * Secondary: **"Open in Panel"**
* If `state == "failed"`: red border, show error and worker log tail; primary button: **"Retry"** (re-spawns forge worker against same `forge_brief.json` — no data lost).

## 6. New Backend Endpoint: Forge Status

`GET /api/governance/forge/<forge_session_id>/status` — looks up the forge worker by session id, returns process state + ADS-derived progress (`cross_ai_progress_update` events filtered to this session) + spec_count (from filesystem scan).

## 7. ADS Schema Additions

`adt_core/ads/schema.py` — extend `FORGE_EVENTS` or add:

```python
FORGE_EVENTS = [
    "forge_initiated",          # path, intent, name
    "forge_brief_written",      # forge_session_id, fields_count
    "forge_worker_spawned",     # forge_session_id, pid
    "forge_vision_filled",      # forge_session_id, spec_id="SPEC-001"
    "forge_child_spec_created", # forge_session_id, spec_id, title
    "forge_complete",           # forge_session_id, spec_ids
    "forge_failed",             # forge_session_id, reason, log_path
]
```

| `ADT_FORGE_MIN_CHILDREN` | 3    | Floor on child spec count |
| `ADT_FORGE_MAX_CHILDREN` | 7    | Ceiling on child spec count |

## 9. Affected Paths

| Path | Role | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `adt-console/src/js/launcher.js` | Frontend | §1 two-screen wizard; §5 progress polling |
| `adt-console/src/css/launcher.css` | Frontend | progress bar + complete/failed states |
| `adt_center/api/governance_routes.py` | Backend | §2 forge endpoint extension; §4 spec-create endpoint; §6 status endpoint |
| `adt_center/api/forge_prompts/architect.md` | Backend | NEW — Phase A + B prompt template |
| `adt_core/ads/schema.py` | Backend | §7 FORGE_EVENTS constant |
| `_cortex/templates/project_bootstrap/SPEC-001_VISION.md.tmpl` | Architect | Leave intact — the worker overwrites it after scaffold |

## 10. Acceptance Criteria

* ✅ Operator submits wizard with eyetoy wish → within 90s sees "Forge Complete: SPEC-001, SPEC-002, SPEC-003, SPEC-004, SPEC-005 created".
* ✅ Opening SPEC-001 in spec map shows filled Problem/Vision/Users/Scope/Success sections (no `TODO:` strings).
* ✅ Opening any child spec shows a one-paragraph Intent and Success Condition that traces to SPEC-001 §5.
* ✅ Pressing Decompose on a child spec produces *technical* tasks (e.g. "implement camera capture pipeline"), not meta tasks ("write Problem section").
* ✅ Forge worker death (timeout, exit-1, killed) surfaces in wizard as red Failed state with log tail.
* ✅ Retry button on Failed state re-runs the worker without re-asking for inputs.

## 11. Rollout

Single phase, single PR — frontend + backend land together because the wizard depends on the new endpoints.

1. Backend: forge endpoint extension + spec-create + status (§2, §4, §6, §7).
2. Prompt template (§3).
3. Frontend: 2-screen wizard + live progress (§1, §5).
4. Smoke test: eyetoy wish → 5 specs created → spec map renders → child decompose produces technical tasks.

ETA: 6-8 hours focused.

## 12. Out of Scope (deferred)

* Operator editing of generated specs in the wizard itself — they can edit in the Panel afterwards.
* Auto-triggering decompose on each child spec — kept manual for v1 so operator reviews specs before tasks fan out.
* Sub-children (SPEC-002 spawning SPEC-002a/b) — keep tree flat for v1.
* Multi-architect contention (two forges at once on same path) — UI prevents this by checking project existence before spawn.

## 13. Cross-Spec Impact

* **SPEC-043 (Forge):** §2 extends the existing endpoint without breaking the old contract (new fields are optional).
* **SPEC-049 (CAOP):** the forge worker can reuse the CAOP task plumbing for progress reporting.
* **SPEC-062 D5 (Task creation):** unchanged — wizard creates specs only, not tasks.
* **SPEC-062-F (Verification):** child specs each gain `acceptance_criteria` placeholders the verifier will later check.
* **SPEC-064 (Standards):** out of scope here — operator can add `standards_refs[]` to any spec after forging.

3. **Return immediately** with `{forge_session_id, project_name, status: "forging"}` — UI now polls progress instead of seeing a static success modal.

## 3. Forge Architect Prompt Template

NEW file `adt_center/api/forge_prompts/architect.md` (template format same as `decompose_prompts/architect.md`).

Two-phase prompt:

**Phase A — Fill SPEC-001:**

* Read `_cortex/ops/forge_brief.json` for the 5 inputs.
* Overwrite `_cortex/specs/SPEC-001_VISION.md` (currently template) with a filled version:
  * §1 Problem: 1 short paragraph extracted from `intent_description`
  * §2 Vision: 1 paragraph end-state description
  * §3 Users: from `users` field, ASCII bullets
  * §4 In Scope: 3-5 bullets derived from wish
  * §4 Out of Scope: from `out_of_scope` field (verbatim if provided; sensible defaults if not)
  * §5 Success Criteria: from `success_v1` field, restated as 2-4 observable checks
  * §6 Constraints: from `constraints` field (verbatim if provided)
  * §7 Open Questions: 2-4 honest unknowns the worker spotted while writing the above
* POST a `cross_ai_progress_update` ADS event: `{phase: "vision_filled", pct: 40}`.

**Phase B — Derive child specs:**

* Identify 3-7 child concerns that, together, deliver the §5 Success Criteria. Examples for eyetoy:
  * SPEC-002: Camera + Vision Pipeline
  * SPEC-003: Hand / Object Tracking
  * SPEC-004: Render Surface + Physics
  * SPEC-005: Game Loop + State
  * (optional) SPEC-006: Onboarding + Calibration
* For EACH child, run one curl against the spec-create endpoint (see §4):

```bash
curl -s -X POST 'http://localhost:5001/api/specs?project={project_name}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{{"spec_id":"SPEC-NNN","title":"...","intent":"<1 paragraph>","success_condition":"<observable test>","tier":"Operational","derived_from":"SPEC-001"}}'
```

* Between child specs, POST `cross_ai_progress_update` with monotonically increasing pct.
* When all children created, POST `cross_ai_task_complete` with `{result_summary, spec_ids_created}`.

The worker does NOT decompose any spec into tasks — that's a separate flow the operator triggers later. The wizard's job ends at "specs created."

## 4. New Backend Endpoint: Create Spec

`POST /api/specs` — accepts `{spec_id, title, intent, success_condition, tier, derived_from}`, writes `_cortex/specs/<spec_id>_<TITLE_UNDERSCORED>.md` with the project's spec markdown format, updates `config/specs.json`, emits `spec_created` ADS event.

If `spec_id` is omitted, server allocates the next free SPEC-NNN.

# SPEC-061 Amendment A: Harness-Agnostic Role Sessions

**Status:** APPROVED
**Author:** Systems_Architect (CLAUDE)
**Date:** 2026-06-18
**Approved:** 2026-06-20 (Systems_Architect, CLAUDE)
**Amends:** SPEC-061 (Antigravity Multi-Model Worker Plane)
**Tier:** Operational
**Priority:** HIGH — without this, SA is the only role NOT freed from a single vendor

**Intent:** Loosen the SPEC-061 harness restriction so that any ADT role — including `Systems_Architect` — can run on either the `claude` (Claude Code) harness OR the `antigravity` (`agy`) harness, with the operator selecting harness + model at session spawn time. The `adt-bridge` plugin ships ADT role definitions as first-class `agy` agents, so spawning an Architect session via `agy --agent architect --model "Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)"` produces a fully ADT-bootstrapped SA session indistinguishable in behavior from the current Claude-Code-summoned one. The Console exposes a "Spawn New Session" modal that surfaces the full role × harness × model matrix.

**Triggering Event:** CEV-AG-003 — Operator request 2026-06-18: "be sure that we are able to start a proper session of agy within adt console as it has claude now if needed, so it can be a sys architect". The motivating insight: because `agy` can host Claude Opus/Sonnet under one Google subscription, the entire ADT control plane (including SA) can run vendor-agnostic. Pinning SA to Claude Code (as SPEC-061 §2.4 currently does) re-introduces the single-vendor dependency the parent spec was designed to remove.

**Success Condition:** From the Console "Spawn New Session" modal, the operator picks (Role = Systems_Architect, Harness = antigravity, Model = Claude Opus 4.6 Thinking) and a new SA session starts. The session loads the constitution, AI_PROTOCOL, MASTER_PLAN, and last 20 ADS events at startup (same bootstrap as `/hive-architect`), can write to `_cortex/` (DTCP allows per SA jurisdiction), and is reachable from other workers' steering inbox at `_cortex/comms/agy_inbox/<session_id>.jsonl`. The existing `/hive-architect` Claude path remains a peer option, not the only one.

---

## 1. Harness Defaults — Loosened

Replace SPEC-061 §2.4 `ROLE_HARNESS_DEFAULTS` with a default that still favors Claude for the SA role (preserves current behavior) but treats it as a default, not a constraint:

```python
ROLE_HARNESS_DEFAULTS = {
    "Systems_Architect": "claude",        # default; antigravity also valid
    "Backend_Engineer":  "antigravity",
    "Frontend_Engineer": "antigravity",
    "DevOps_Engineer":   "antigravity",
    "Overseer":          "antigravity",
    "All":               "antigravity",
}
ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED = {
    "Systems_Architect": {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Backend_Engineer":  {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Frontend_Engineer": {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "DevOps_Engineer":   {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Overseer":          {"claude", "antigravity"},
}
```

Task-level `harness` override is validated against `ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED[role]`. The build executor refuses any unallowed combination with `build_blocked{error: "harness_role_unauthorized"}`.

## 2. ADT Role Definitions in the Plugin

Extend the `adt-bridge` plugin manifest (SPEC-061 §1.2) with `agents[]`:

```json
{
  "name": "adt-bridge",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "agents": [
    "agents/architect/AGENT.md",
    "agents/backend/AGENT.md",
    "agents/frontend/AGENT.md",
    "agents/devops/AGENT.md",
    "agents/overseer/AGENT.md"
  ],
  "hooks": ["hooks/pre_tool.py", "hooks/post_tool.py", "hooks/stop.py"]
}
```

Each `AGENT.md` follows the agy agent-persona format (frontmatter + body) and embeds the ADT bootstrap sequence currently in the corresponding `/hive-*` Hivemind skill. The architect agent specifically:

* Reads `_cortex/AI_PROTOCOL.md`, `_cortex/MASTER_PLAN.md`, and the last 20 ADS events on startup.
* Sets `ADT_ROLE=Systems_Architect`, `ADT_AGENT=ANTIGRAVITY` in its persona-injected environment.
* Logs `session_start` via DTCP `/log`.
* Honors the same jurisdiction rules as Claude-summoned SA (writes to `_cortex/`, blocked elsewhere).

## 3. SA Session Bootstrap on `agy`

A new SA session is invoked as:

```
agy --agent architect --model "Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)" -p "Begin session as ADT Systems_Architect."
```

The plugin's PreInvocation hook (NEW slot in the manifest; see SPEC-061 §1 — `PreInvocationHook` is one of the lifecycle hooks observable in the agy binary) injects the constitution, master plan, and recent ADS events into the system context before the model's first turn. This replaces the file-reading bootstrap in step 1-7 of the existing `/hive-architect` skill.

If the PreInvocation hook is unavailable in agy's plugin lifecycle (open question §6.1 below), the fallback is a pre-seeded prompt: the dispatcher reads the bootstrap files itself and prepends them to the `-p` prompt.

## 4. Console UI — "Spawn New Session" Modal

Replace the implicit "spawn a Claude session" affordance with an explicit modal:

| Field | Options |
|---|---|
| Role | Systems_Architect, Backend_Engineer, Frontend_Engineer, DevOps_Engineer, Overseer |
| Harness | claude, antigravity (filtered by `ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED[role]`) |
| Model | (only shown if harness=antigravity) populated from `agy models` |
| Optional first prompt | freeform textarea |

On submit, the Console POSTs to `POST /api/workers/spawn` with `{role, harness, model, prompt}`. The backend (`adt_center/api/workers_routes.py` from SPEC-061 §3.2) constructs the appropriate command, spawns the PTY, registers the session, and returns `{session_id}` which the Console adds to the Workers tab.

The existing `/hive-architect` slash-command path remains for terminal users; the modal is the GUI equivalent that additionally supports the agy + Claude-Opus combination.

# SPEC-061 Amendment A: Harness-Agnostic Role Sessions

**Status:** APPROVED
**Author:** Systems_Architect (CLAUDE)
**Date:** 2026-06-18
**Approved:** 2026-06-20 (Systems_Architect, CLAUDE)
**Amends:** SPEC-061 (Antigravity Multi-Model Worker Plane)
**Tier:** Operational
**Priority:** HIGH — without this, SA is the only role NOT freed from a single vendor

**Intent:** Loosen the SPEC-061 harness restriction so that any ADT role — including `Systems_Architect` — can run on either the `claude` (Claude Code) harness OR the `antigravity` (`agy`) harness, with the operator selecting harness + model at session spawn time. The `adt-bridge` plugin ships ADT role definitions as first-class `agy` agents, so spawning an Architect session via `agy --agent architect --model "Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)"` produces a fully ADT-bootstrapped SA session indistinguishable in behavior from the current Claude-Code-summoned one. The Console exposes a "Spawn New Session" modal that surfaces the full role × harness × model matrix.

**Triggering Event:** CEV-AG-003 — Operator request 2026-06-18: "be sure that we are able to start a proper session of agy within adt console as it has claude now if needed, so it can be a sys architect". The motivating insight: because `agy` can host Claude Opus/Sonnet under one Google subscription, the entire ADT control plane (including SA) can run vendor-agnostic. Pinning SA to Claude Code (as SPEC-061 §2.4 currently does) re-introduces the single-vendor dependency the parent spec was designed to remove.

**Success Condition:** From the Console "Spawn New Session" modal, the operator picks (Role = Systems_Architect, Harness = antigravity, Model = Claude Opus 4.6 Thinking) and a new SA session starts. The session loads the constitution, AI_PROTOCOL, MASTER_PLAN, and last 20 ADS events at startup (same bootstrap as `/hive-architect`), can write to `_cortex/` (DTCP allows per SA jurisdiction), and is reachable from other workers' steering inbox at `_cortex/comms/agy_inbox/<session_id>.jsonl`. The existing `/hive-architect` Claude path remains a peer option, not the only one.

---

## 1. Harness Defaults — Loosened

Replace SPEC-061 §2.4 `ROLE_HARNESS_DEFAULTS` with a default that still favors Claude for the SA role (preserves current behavior) but treats it as a default, not a constraint:

```python
ROLE_HARNESS_DEFAULTS = {
    "Systems_Architect": "claude",        # default; antigravity also valid
    "Backend_Engineer":  "antigravity",
    "Frontend_Engineer": "antigravity",
    "DevOps_Engineer":   "antigravity",
    "Overseer":          "antigravity",
    "All":               "antigravity",
}
ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED = {
    "Systems_Architect": {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Backend_Engineer":  {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Frontend_Engineer": {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "DevOps_Engineer":   {"claude", "antigravity"},
    "Overseer":          {"claude", "antigravity"},
}
```

Task-level `harness` override is validated against `ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED[role]`. The build executor refuses any unallowed combination with `build_blocked{error: "harness_role_unauthorized"}`.

## 2. ADT Role Definitions in the Plugin

Extend the `adt-bridge` plugin manifest (SPEC-061 §1.2) with `agents[]`:

```json
{
  "name": "adt-bridge",
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "agents": [
    "agents/architect/AGENT.md",
    "agents/backend/AGENT.md",
    "agents/frontend/AGENT.md",
    "agents/devops/AGENT.md",
    "agents/overseer/AGENT.md"
  ],
  "hooks": ["hooks/pre_tool.py", "hooks/post_tool.py", "hooks/stop.py"]
}
```

Each `AGENT.md` follows the agy agent-persona format (frontmatter + body) and embeds the ADT bootstrap sequence currently in the corresponding `/hive-*` Hivemind skill. The architect agent specifically:

* Reads `_cortex/AI_PROTOCOL.md`, `_cortex/MASTER_PLAN.md`, and the last 20 ADS events on startup.
* Sets `ADT_ROLE=Systems_Architect`, `ADT_AGENT=ANTIGRAVITY` in its persona-injected environment.
* Logs `session_start` via DTCP `/log`.
* Honors the same jurisdiction rules as Claude-summoned SA (writes to `_cortex/`, blocked elsewhere).

## 3. SA Session Bootstrap on `agy`

A new SA session is invoked as:

```
agy --agent architect --model "Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)" -p "Begin session as ADT Systems_Architect."
```

The plugin's PreInvocation hook (NEW slot in the manifest; see SPEC-061 §1 — `PreInvocationHook` is one of the lifecycle hooks observable in the agy binary) injects the constitution, master plan, and recent ADS events into the system context before the model's first turn. This replaces the file-reading bootstrap in step 1-7 of the existing `/hive-architect` skill.

If the PreInvocation hook is unavailable in agy's plugin lifecycle (open question §6.1 below), the fallback is a pre-seeded prompt: the dispatcher reads the bootstrap files itself and prepends them to the `-p` prompt.

## 4. Console UI — "Spawn New Session" Modal

Replace the implicit "spawn a Claude session" affordance with an explicit modal:

| Field | Options |
|---|---|
| Role | Systems_Architect, Backend_Engineer, Frontend_Engineer, DevOps_Engineer, Overseer |
| Harness | claude, antigravity (filtered by `ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED[role]`) |
| Model | (only shown if harness=antigravity) populated from `agy models` |
| Optional first prompt | freeform textarea |

On submit, the Console POSTs to `POST /api/workers/spawn` with `{role, harness, model, prompt}`. The backend (`adt_center/api/workers_routes.py` from SPEC-061 §3.2) constructs the appropriate command, spawns the PTY, registers the session, and returns `{session_id}` which the Console adds to the Workers tab.

The existing `/hive-architect` slash-command path remains for terminal users; the modal is the GUI equivalent that additionally supports the agy + Claude-Opus combination.

| Path | Role | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/agents/architect/AGENT.md` | Backend | new |
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/agents/backend/AGENT.md` | Backend | new |
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/agents/frontend/AGENT.md` | Backend | new |
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/agents/devops/AGENT.md` | Backend | new |
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/agents/overseer/AGENT.md` | Backend | new |
| `adt_sdk/plugins/adt-bridge/hooks/pre_invocation.py` | Backend | new (if agy supports it) |
| `adt_center/api/workers_routes.py` | Backend | add `POST /api/workers/spawn` endpoint |
| `adt_center/api/build_executor.py` | Backend | add `ROLE_HARNESS_ALLOWED` validation |
| `adt-console/src/js/workers.js` | Frontend | new "Spawn New Session" modal |
| `adt-console/src/index.html` | Frontend | modal markup |
| `adt-console/src-tauri/src/pty.rs` | DevOps | spawn helper accepts role/harness/model args |

## 6. Open Questions

1. **PreInvocation hook availability:** Binary symbols show `PreInvocationHook` exists, but its exact lifecycle position (before model's first turn? before plugin agents load?) needs the §6.1 probe to confirm. If unavailable, §3 fallback applies.
2. **Agent invocation syntax:** Whether `agy --agent <name>` is the actual flag, or if agents are selected via slash command in interactive mode, or via a `default_agent` plugin field. To verify in probe phase.
3. **Self-summoning:** Can an `agy`-hosted SA session itself spawn worker sessions? It needs to call `POST /api/workers/spawn` — confirms that the bridge's HTTP client can reach `adt_center` from inside the sandbox. Already true for the DTCP path, so likely fine.

## 7. Rollout Impact

Insert between SPEC-061 phases 6.2 and 6.3:

* **6.2.5 — Plugin agents (Backend):** Author the five `AGENT.md` files. The architect agent is the load-bearing one; others can be stubs initially that just set role env vars and rely on the existing summon skills' content.

Insert after SPEC-061 phase 6.5:

* **6.5.5 — Spawn modal (Frontend):** Implement §4 modal. This unlocks operator-driven session creation without command-line summoning.

No phase is moved or removed; this amendment strictly adds capability.

Spec : SPEC-070 Jurisdiction (files you may edit): ., Cargo.toml, Makefile, README.md, _cortex/capabilities/capability_events.jsonl, _cortex/work_logs/, adt_center/api/, adt_center/api/governance_routes.py, adt_center/app.py, adt_center/services/, adt_core/, adt_core/ads/schema.py, adt_core/standards/, adt_sdk/, app.py, assets/, config/, css/, docker-compose.yml, docs/, index.html, js/, main.py, package.json, public/, requirements.txt, src/, static/, tests/, tests/integration/ --- SPEC CONTENT --- # SPEC-070: Mirror Mode Screenshot Stream (Assistant Monitor Panel) **Status:** APPROVED **Author:** Systems_Architect (CLAUDE, on operator direction) **Date:** 2026-07-04 **Amends:** SPEC-069 (Mirror Mode); complements SPEC-062 (Spec Skill Tree Map) **Tier:** Operational **Priority:** HIGH — operator can currently DRIVE Paul's console (mirror clicks + inputs + ack roundtrip) but has no visual confirmation that Paul's UI is actually reflecting the mirrored actions. A 0.5 Hz screenshot stream closes that gap without the cost of a full video RDP layer. **Intent:** When Mirror Mode is active on the operator's console, Paul's adt_center captures a screenshot of the adt-console window every 2 seconds and pushes it to the operator's adt_center. The operator's frontend shows those frames in a floating Assistant Monitor panel — minimizable/expandable, with a 1 fps monitor frame — so the operator visually verifies the mirror is landing correctly, sees dialogs Paul is looking at, and catches drift the ack channel cannot (e.g. modal opened but wrong data, layout broken, browser popup obscuring the target). **Triggering Event:** CEV-OP-014 — 2026-07-04 operator note. Text-based click acks confirm target existed and was clicked, but do not reveal UI-level surprises (permission popup covering the button, wrong project loaded, spec map focused on wrong node). A cheap visual channel closes the loop. **Success Condition:** With Mirror Mode ON and Paul's console open, the operator's Assistant Monitor panel updates a new JPEG frame within 2.5 s of capture, sustained for the duration of the mirror session. Frames are captured only when Mirror is active (no idle capture). Panel minimize/expand + position persists across page reloads via localStorage. Peer network path is Tailscale-only; no capture leaves the tailnet. --- ## 1. Stack - **Peer capture (Paul's adt_center):** Python 3 + `mss` (cross-platform screenshot via ctypes; no X11-tools dependency, works on WSLg/Wayland/Xorg). Fallback: shell out to `import -window ` (ImageMagick). - **Transport:** HTTP POST binary body (`image/jpeg`) over Tailscale to operator's adt_center. No WebSocket, no base64 (payload ~50 KB per frame). - **Operator receiver (my adt_center):** Flask blueprint route + in-memory ring buffer keyed by `(peer_id, session_id)`. - **Frontend (adt-console/src):** vanilla JS floating panel with `` element polled at 2 s. CSS resize/minimize; localStorage-persisted position + collapsed state. ## 2. Files to Create - `adt_center/services/mirror_screenshot_capture.py` (~180 lines) - `adt-console/src/js/mirror_monitor.js` (~200 lines) ## 3. Files to Modify - `adt_center/api/governance_routes.py` — add 3 endpoints; ~60 lines - `adt-console/src/index.html` — register `mirror_monitor.js` before `spec_map.js`; ~2 lines - `adt-console/src/js/mirror.js` — on toggle-on, POST `mirror_capture_start` command to peer; on toggle-off, `mirror_capture_stop` (~10 lines) - `adt-console/src/js/remote.js` — dispatch new commands `mirror_capture_start` / `mirror_capture_stop` to a local endpoint on the peer's adt_center (~15 lines) ## 4. API Surface ### 4.1 On Paul's (peer) adt_center ```python # adt_center/services/mirror_screenshot_capture.py class MirrorScreenshotCapture: """Grabs frames of the adt-console window and POSTs each to the operator's collector at collector_url. Started/stopped via /api/mirror/capture routes. Idempotent start (second start is no-op).""" CAPTURE_INTERVAL_SEC = 2 JPEG_QUALITY = 60 MAX_LONG_EDGE_PX = 1600 # downscale before send if wider def __init__(self, collector_url: str, peer_id: str, session_id: str) -> None: ... def start(self) -> None: ... def stop(self) -> None: ... def status(self) -> dict: # {running: bool, frames_sent: int, last_error: str|None, last_sent_at: float|None} ... def _find_console_window_id(self) -> Optional[str]: """Return X11 window id for the adt-console window (via xdotool or wmctrl). Returns None if not found; capture falls back to full screen.""" def _capture_frame(self) -> bytes: """Return JPEG bytes of the current console window (or full screen). Uses mss if available, else shells to `import -window `.""" def _post_frame(self, jpeg: bytes) -> None: """POST to collector_url with headers X-Peer-Id, X-Session-Id, X-Frame-Ts (unix ms). Body is raw image/jpeg. 5s timeout, fire and forget.""" ``` New Flask routes on Paul's adt_center: - `POST /api/mirror/capture/start` — body `{collector_url, peer_id, session_id}` → starts capture thread; returns `{status:"started", running:true}`. - `POST /api/mirror/capture/stop` — stops thread; returns `{status:"stopped", frames_sent:N}`. - `GET /api/mirror/capture/status` — returns capture status dict. ### 4.2 On the operator's adt_center (receiver) ```python # In adt_center/api/governance_routes.py _MIRROR_FRAMES = {} # (peer_id, session_id) -> {jpeg: bytes, ts: float, seq: int} _MIRROR_FRAMES_SEQ = 0 _MIRROR_FRAMES_LOCK = threading.Lock() @governance_bp.route("/mirror/frame", methods=["POST"]) def api_mirror_frame_recv(): """Peer POSTs the latest JPEG here. Overwrites the previous frame for the (peer_id, session_id) key. Cheap: no persistence, RAM only.""" @governance_bp.route("/mirror/frame/latest", methods=["GET"]) def api_mirror_frame_latest(): """Return the latest JPEG (or 204 No Content). Query: peer_id, session_id. Response is image/jpeg with X-Frame-Ts + X-Frame-Age-Ms headers so the frontend can show freshness.""" ``` ### 4.3 Frontend Assistant Monitor panel ```js // adt-console/src/js/mirror_monitor.js window.MirrorMonitor = { init(): void, // creates panel DOM once show(): void, // makes visible + starts poll hide(): void, // hides + stops poll minimize(): void, // collapses to title bar expand(): void, // restores full frame setPeer({peer_id, session_id, collector_url}): void, // called by mirror.js on toggle status(): {polling:bool, frames_shown:int, last_frame_age_ms:number|null}, }; ``` Panel structure: - Fixed-position `div` (default: top-right, 320×240 px, draggable by header). - Title bar with `[🔎 Peer: pauls] [⤢ expand] [– minimize] [× close]`. - `` element updates every 2 s from `GET /api/mirror/frame/latest?peer_id=...&session_id=...`. - Below image: 10 px status strip showing `Frame age: 1.4 s` (green <3 s, yellow <10 s, red >10 s). - Position + minimized state persisted to `localStorage['adt_mirror_monitor_state']`. ## 5. Acceptance Criteria (observable) **AC-70-1 (Endpoint availability):** On Paul's adt_center, `POST /api/mirror/capture/start` with valid body returns HTTP 200 with `running:true`; `GET /api/mirror/capture/status` returns the same. On operator's adt_center, `GET /api/mirror/frame/latest?peer_id=pauls&session_id=X` returns HTTP 204 before any frame is received. **AC-70-2 (Capture roundtrip < 2.5 s):** Given Mirror ON on operator side and Paul's console visible, within 3 s the operator's `/api/mirror/frame/latest` returns HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` body. Repeated for at least 30 consecutive requests over 60 s — each request returns a fresh frame (X-Frame-Ts increases monotonically). **AC-70-3 (Panel renders live):** The Assistant Monitor panel `` src has its cache-busted URL updated at least once per 2.5 s while polling is active. Panel remains stable during scroll / spec-map interactions. **AC-70-4 (Auto start/stop with Mirror):** When operator toggles Mirror OFF, Paul's `MirrorScreenshotCapture.stop()` is invoked within 5 s (verified by tail of Paul's log showing `capture stopped`) and operator's frontend stops polling. `_MIRROR_FRAMES` entry for that key remains for 10 min then is GC'd; new toggle-ON creates a fresh session key. **AC-70-5 (Minimize/expand persists):** Operator minimizes the panel; reloads the console; the panel reopens in the minimized state. Same for panel position (drag it, reload, position preserved). **AC-70-6 (Frame size budget):** Median frame size ≤ 80 KB after JPEG quality 60 + 1600 px long-edge downscale. p95 ≤ 120 KB. Verified by capturing 60 s of frames and inspecting bytes-received on the operator. **AC-70-7 (No capture when idle):** With Mirror OFF, `MirrorScreenshotCapture` thread is NOT running on Paul's adt_center (verified: `pgrep -af mirror_screenshot_capture` returns empty; `/api/mirror/capture/status` returns `running:false`). **AC-70-8 (Fallback capture works):** If `mss` is missing on Paul's system, `_capture_frame` falls back to shelling `import -window `. On a system without either, capture returns a placeholder 640×480 JPEG containing the text "capture unavailable" + last error; the panel shows the placeholder and a warning strip. ## 6. Reads From - SPEC-069 (Mirror Mode) — extends the peer command channel + ack pipeline - SPEC-062-D (Operator Actions) — reuses the highlight overlay style for the monitor panel border - SPEC-036 (Sandbox) — the capture service runs unsandboxed; must NOT be sandboxed since it needs raw access to the display ## 7. Non-Goals - No audio capture, no mouse cursor overlay in the frames. - No video encoding (H.264, WebM). Static JPEG frames are enough at 0.5 fps. - No storage of frames on disk (RAM-only ring; on-restart the buffer is empty). - No multi-peer support in v1 (one peer at a time; multi-peer is a follow-up). - No screenshot editing / annotation. - Not a replacement for full-blown RDP / VNC; just a diagnostic feed. ## 8. Security & Privacy - Capture only starts when the operator toggles Mirror ON. The peer's console shows the MIRROR RECEIVER banner during capture (SPEC-069 already implements this). - Collector URL is provided at start; peer will not stream to unknown endpoints. - Frames are in-flight only (no persistent storage on either end). - Tailscale is the sole transport; refuse `collector_url` that is not on the tailnet subnet (100.64.0.0/10). ## 9. Rollout & Rollback - Feature-flagged in Paul's adt_center: env var `ADT_MIRROR_CAPTURE_DISABLED=1` short-circuits `/api/mirror/capture/start` to return HTTP 501 immediately. - Frontend: if the receiver returns 204 for 30 s continuously, the panel shows "waiting for peer…" and stops re-fetching until the next toggle. - Rollback: setting `ADT_MIRROR_CAPTURE_DISABLED=1` on Paul + refreshing operator's console disables the whole flow with no other changes. --- END SPEC --- YOUR ASSIGNED TASKS: [task_458] Create screenshot capture service on peer Implement the MirrorScreenshotCapture service class in adt_center/services/mirror_screenshot_capture.py that handles periodic capture using mss or import fallback and posts to the collector URL.
